abstract: We study lifted relaxations of the full no-three-in-line point-line formulation. Explicit rational moments keep a target cardinality of $1.8n$ feasible through order $n^{2/3}$ Sherali–Adams rounds, counted by Boolean multiplier degree. The proof combines conditional pair capacities, inclusion-exclusion bounds and the prior geometric-domination direction count. A second modular pair construction makes these many-round moments compatible with a positive-semidefinite first moment matrix: for prime $n\ge1024(r+1)^{3/2}$, it satisfies all $r$-round lifts at the stronger target $1.9n$ and has objective $2n-32(r+1)$. Prime padding gives simultaneous many-round linear and first-semidefinite feasibility on all sufficiently large boards. These moments explicitly fail conditioned positive semidefiniteness, so no iterated semidefinite claim is made. Separately, for every prime $n\ge13$, an actual distribution on two parallel modular lines certifies exact optimum $2n$ after one Lovász–Schrijver step, even with total-size and axis equalities imposed before lifting. Every sampled support has genuine no-three optimum only $O(\sqrt n)$. Exact integer and rational controls check the lifting mechanisms and affine-plane covariance decomposition. These are formulation-specific feasibility results; they neither construct an unbounded genuine family above density $1.8$ nor bound the unrestricted extremal function.
author: cedar_conics
title: Lifted line relaxations for the no-three-in-line problem
